# World Civilizations Explorer

> A source-grounded, AI-assisted guide to 10,000 years of human history —
> civilizations, historical figures, topics, eras, interactive maps, and
> timelines. Content is built on public, attributable sources and rendered as
> clean, crawlable HTML.

## What this site is
World Civilizations Explorer helps people explore world history through
structured, cross-linked pages for civilizations, the people who shaped them,
the topics that defined them, and the eras they belong to. It combines
encyclopedic text, museum artifacts, primary sources, maps, and timelines.

## Main sections
- /civilizations — Index of every civilization (Ancient, Medieval, Modern).
- /civilizations/{slug} — A civilization guide: summary, key facts, timeline,
  key figures, topics, gallery, museum artifacts, and primary sources.
- /figures — Index of notable historical figures.
- /figures/{slug} — A figure's biography, timeline, and related civilizations.
- /topics/{slug} — A topic's overview, related civilizations, figures, and sources.
- /era/{ancient|medieval|modern} — Civilizations and milestones within an era.
- /timeline — Interactive timeline across all civilizations.
- /map — Interactive world history map.
- /compare — Side-by-side comparison of two civilizations.
- /museums — Search artifacts from world museum collections.
- /ask — Source-grounded AI Q&A about history.
- /sources — Data providers and attribution policy.

## Data source policy
Content is grounded in public, attributable sources, including: Wikipedia,
Wikimedia Commons, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Rijksmuseum, the Art
Institute of Chicago, and the Library of Congress. Source/provenance labels are
shown in readable text on the pages themselves. Historical imagery comes from
Wikimedia/museum collections; modern location photography may come from
Unsplash and is not used as a substitute for historical artifacts.

## Source-grounding & AI labeling rules
- Factual content is grounded in the sources above; we do not fabricate
  historical facts, citations, or images.
- AI-assisted text (such as generated timelines and the /ask answers) is
  labeled as AI-assisted and remains grounded in retrieved sources.
- Structured data (JSON-LD) on each page reflects the visible page content.

## Machine-readable surfaces
- Sitemap: /sitemap.xml
- Robots: /robots.txt
